feature: Idle saved SDK branch cloning with independent native contexts

red.finding: The existing SDK history guard cancelled a normal Pi clone.

retainedDevelopmentFailure.finding: Repeated Pi RPC fork-start events overwrote the first valid clone receipt with a rejected second receipt. Receipt creation is now idempotent for the target session; invalid receipts are never silently repaired.

replayE2E.fixture: Real Pi clone/RPC/persistence, SDK provider, MCP, permissions, validation and counted effects; only the external SDK peer is replayed
assertions: Original file remains byte-identical during cloning and clone-only work
Source and clone recall independent values after restart
Different active native session IDs; each subsequently resumes its own checkpoint
SIGKILL only the owned worker after receipt and before the first clone checkpoint; continuation succeeds after restart
An unactivated clone can be cloned or compacted while keeping its original configuration owner bound
Compaction before cloning does not confuse its shorter projection with the old configuration boundary
Moving the parent after publication does not prevent the clone's own restart
A rejected busy clone leaves its source running
Missing/altered receipts, source, configuration or ownership reject before another SDK query
Unknown SDK work, missing results and pending input cannot be approved by cloning
New calls preserve normal Pi permissions and argument validation
Historical call IDs cannot execute again
Usage totals include copied historical usage and new work without reusing the parent's native reported baseline

liveSharedContract.fixture: Real Codex/SDK models, normal personal settings/instructions/extensions, isolated host/projects/sessions and mobile Chromium
assertions: Identical normal parent tool sets across all three models
Marker first obtained by an executed tool reading a file, not supplied in the prompt
One counted filesystem effect before cloning; neither branch repeats tools
Actual Pi clone through RPC, then both files reopened through mobile UI
Original bytes unchanged by creating and using the clone
Each branch learns its own value and retains it without revealing the other branch's value
Both branches repeat correct memory after replacing their owned workers
Active SDK native IDs differ between source and clone and stay stable within each branch after restart
The inherited parent checkpoint remains copied audit data, not the clone's resume target
Matching call/result IDs and reconciled nonnegative token usage
Personal settings bytes unchanged; owned workers closed
liveSharedContract.note: Haiku used one bash call for the append and file read. Codex and Opus used bash plus read. The observable contract and normal tools were the same; no fixed tool sequence or restricted profile was substituted.

compactionRegression.addedCase: A receipt with accepted SDK work cannot replace its configuration with null. The shared validator rejects it before SDK startup.

notVerifiedOrEnabled: Ephemeral/in-flight cloning or unknown uncheckpointed SDK work
Child-local clone/resume lifecycle and nested delegation
Every partial-file/power-loss boundary and long-running stress
privacy: Artifact paths are local temporary-directory basenames. Raw prompts, sessions, tool payloads, browser traces and native transcripts stay private.
